In education and in any learning process, the instructor plays a critical role. Not everyone who has knowledge can teach; not everyone who teaches truly understands the subject; and not everyone who both knows and teaches knows how to teach effectively. Unfortunately, in this case, the instructor failed significantly in fulfilling that role.

First, despite this being a course delivered in Spanish, the instructor persistently relied on an improvised and poorly executed use of English terminology. This “invented” English was not only incorrect, but also became a constant distraction, seriously undermining the audience's ability to follow the content in a focused and rigorous manner.

Second, the pace of delivery was excessively slow and monotonous, reaching a level of repetitiveness that made sustained attention unnecessarily difficult. A measured pace is valuable, but in this instance it crossed into an almost paralyzing lethargy that detracted from the learning experience.

Third, live programming sessions are meant to be interactive and practical, allowing participants to follow along and work in parallel with the instructor. They should not be purely narrative. When participants cannot actively engage or later access a recording, such sessions become inefficient and result in a significant loss of time rather than meaningful learning.

Overall, this was a disappointing experience. With better linguistic choices, a more dynamic delivery, and a clearer understanding of how to conduct effective live instruction, the course could have achieved its objectives. As it stands, it fell well short of expectations.

Ineffective communication and misuse of language
 If you selected 'Other' please provide details.
It is important to clarify that the instructor's technical knowledge is not in question. On the contrary, they clearly possess a strong and deep understanding of the subject. However, expertise alone is not sufficient in an educational context. There is a marked lack of didactic skill and of an understanding of how to effectively transmit knowledge so that it becomes meaningful, clear, and enduring for learners. The excessive and incorrect use of English terminology—despite the course being delivered in Spanish—reflects this gap. This was not a matter of lacking English proficiency, but of failing to communicate in clear, simple Spanish when that was both possible and appropriate. Choosing to use flawed English expressions instead of precise Spanish terminology unnecessarily disrupted the learning process and detracted from the instructor's otherwise solid command of the material.
